- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak values by 2–5%.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.3) or neutral, model often underestimates; increase forecast lows by 2–5% to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > +5% above recent mean), model frequently overcorrects; cap subsequent forecast increases at +3% to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive, model lags in adjusting; delay forecast rise by 1–2 days or add 1–2% buffer to avoid premature recovery.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 70), model tends to hold high forecasts; reduce 30d forecast mean by 3–5% to reflect downward bias.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model exhibits high volatility bias; smooth 30d forecast with 3–5% dampening to reduce overfitting to noise.
